answer.evidence: The head (rows 0-13) is a round disc seen face-on. Its silhouette widens from 7 to 15 px and narrows again to 6 px, but that is the outline of a vertical mirror face. It is not a horizontal cap plate seen from above. The orange hood (rows 1-4) with a dark line at row 5 reads as a thin visor or rim, and the blue mirror face and green stripe below it are vertical. The pole (5 px wide, rows 14-27) is a plain vertical shaft. The base (rows 27-31) has a 1-row light top edge at row 28 and no real top surface. No part of the column shows a top surface that overhangs the shaft.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a pole-mounted curve mirror with an orange rim, a blue-grey glass face, a post and a small base. It sits at the same scale as the references and is a plausible standing prop. Measured facts support it: 18 visible tones per tile, against 17 for the cheese stall, 20 for the roofed well and 9 for the hedge. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills of about 5x5 pixels or more. None of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline carries a tint. By eye, the rim and post are outlined in dark brown or rust rather than black, and the mirror face and post show about 4-5 steps of shading with highlight dots. Texture is moderate, as expected for a thin prop, and it does not look noticeably thinner or flatter than the lamp or the bench. It is slightly simpler than the stall and well, but this is a single-pole prop and the facts are at the reference level.

answer.evidence: This is a curve mirror on a pole. The head spans rows 0-13 and its width profile widens (7 to 15) and then narrows (to 6 at row 14), so its silhouette is an ellipse over a 5px shaft. The mirror face (rows 6-13) is a face-on vertical disc. The only top-like surface is the orange hood, rows 1-4: it ends in a darker front-edge line at row 4 and is followed by a dark eave-shadow row at row 5. The shaft is a 5px pole in rows 15-26, and the base slab at rows 27-31 has a lighter top row at row 28. The pole and base give a front face well over 3 rows. The top surface is thin (4 rows) and the disc itself is drawn face-on, so this is a borderline three_quarter reading.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a thin curve-mirror prop: an orange rim around a pale mirror face, a short pole and a small base. It is drawn at the same scale as the references, so judging by eye against the lamp and well is fair. Measured facts: 18 visible tones per full tile, which matches the cheese stall (17) and the roofed well (20) and is well above the hedge (9). Near-flat coverage is 0%. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is a tinted dark version of the neighbouring rim and pole colours, not a black sticker line. The rim, mirror face and pole each show about 4-5 lightness steps with highlight and shadow dots. The mirror face has a gradient, not a single flat fill. It is simple and has less grain than the stall or well, but it is not thinner or flatter than the lamp-crook reference, and a careful artist would accept it beside the references.
